## Simple explanation

An LSTM is a type of recurrent neural network that carries a memory through a
sequence. Gates let it decide what information to keep, add, or expose at each
step, helping it learn dependencies that span many time steps.

## Technical explanation

At time step $t$, an LSTM combines the current input $x_t$, previous hidden
state $h_{t-1}$, and previous cell state $c_{t-1}$. It computes a forget gate
$f_t$, input gate $i_t$, candidate cell content $\tilde{c}_t$, and output
gate $o_t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_t &= \sigma(W_f [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_f) \\
i_t &= \sigma(W_i [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_i) \\
\tilde{c}_t &= \tanh(W_c [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_c) \\
c_t &= f_t \odot c_{t-1} + i_t \odot \tilde{c}_t \\
o_t &= \sigma(W_o [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_o) \\
h_t &= o_t \odot \tanh(c_t)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $\sigma$ is the sigmoid function, $[\cdot,\cdot]$ concatenates vectors,
and $\odot$ is element-wise multiplication. The cell state provides a path for
information to persist through the sequence.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

LSTMs helped make recurrent models effective for language, time series, and
other sequential data by improving information flow across time. They remain
useful in some settings, although Transformers are now common for many
large-scale sequence tasks.

## How it works

At each step, the forget gate controls how much of the old cell state remains;
the input gate controls how much candidate information is written; and the
output gate controls how much of the cell state becomes the hidden state.

The diagram simplifies the computation: each gate uses both the current input
and previous hidden state, and the cell update combines gated values.

## Practical example

For a sequence of sensor readings, an LSTM can process one reading at a time
and use its hidden state to help predict the next value. The cell state can
retain a pattern that spans several readings.

## Common misconceptions

- LSTM gates learn their behavior from data; they are not manually written rules.
- LSTMs reduce some long-range learning difficulties but do not guarantee that arbitrarily distant information is retained.
- An LSTM is one recurrent architecture, not a synonym for all sequence models.
